section_summary: This section contains translated transcripts of Tokyo station JLU4 broadcasts from August 11–21, 1941, with FBI cover letters forwarding two groups of transcripts to the State Department. The broadcasts report war news, Japanese operations in China and French Indochina, and responses to the Roosevelt–Churchill declaration. Their commentaries repeatedly portray British and American aid to the Soviet Union, economic restrictions on Japan, and military preparations near Thailand as threats to Japan.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 broadcast transcript, concluding pages
subfiles.about: A broadcast discusses alleged British pressure on Thailand and reports war news from Asia and Europe.
subfiles.summary: The surviving pages continue a commentary accusing Britain of trying to draw Japan and the United States into war over Thailand. News items cover the Thai–French Indochinese boundary talks, Soviet and German fighting, French officers detained in Syria, and U.S. planes sent to the Soviet Union.

subfiles.title: FBI cover letter forwarding Tokyo radio transcripts, August 16–21
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: The FBI forwards translated Tokyo broadcasts for August 16–21, 1941.
subfiles.summary: Forwards translated Tokyo radio transcripts for August 16–21.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, August 21, 1941
subfiles.about: A poorly received broadcast reports diplomatic and war news, then comments on the German–Soviet war.
subfiles.summary: The weak recording covers Manchukuo–Mongolia talks, Allied aid to the Soviet Union, and the Russo-German war.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, August 20, 1941
subfiles.about: News and commentary focus on Anglo-American aid to the Soviet Union and its alleged threat to Japan.
subfiles.summary: News items cover Europe, Thailand, China, and a proposed Manchukuo–Mongolia boundary meeting. A lengthy commentary argues that Anglo-American shipments through Vladivostok and aircraft routes through Alaska and Kamchatka threaten Japan from the north. Wakao Oiwa also praises the Nanjing government and dismisses aid to Chongqing.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, August 19, 1941
subfiles.about: The broadcast presents the proposed Moscow conference as part of an encirclement of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports discuss the proposed Allied–Soviet conference, shipments to Vladivostok, Japanese military operations, conditions in Chongqing and Hong Kong, and joint defense talks in French Indochina. Commentaries contrast the Nanjing and Chongqing governments and describe patriotic training of Japanese schoolchildren.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, August 18, 1941
subfiles.about: The program covers Japanese diplomacy, Allied reaction to the Roosevelt–Churchill declaration, and weekly war news.
subfiles.summary: Reports include Ambassador Nomura’s message to Japanese residents on the U.S. Pacific Coast, criticism of the Roosevelt–Churchill declaration, German war claims, and Japanese appointments. Veteran Eiji Makino speaks about notifying a soldier’s family of his death.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, August 17, 1941
subfiles.about: A lengthy broadcast denounces the Roosevelt–Churchill declaration and reports developments across several war fronts.
subfiles.summary: The news covers Japanese raids in China, discussion of a Moscow conference, the Thai–French Indochinese boundary meeting, fighting in Europe and North Africa, and economic conditions in the United States. The extended commentary calls the eight-point Roosevelt–Churchill declaration a disguise for Anglo-American domination and alleges plans for joint action against Japan.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, August 16, 1941
subfiles.to: Radio audience, including a segment addressed to children in Hawaii
subfiles.about: The broadcast promotes Japanese war preparations and criticizes Allied policy in East Asia.
subfiles.summary: News items cover the Roosevelt–Churchill declaration, Japan’s diplomatic ties with Thailand, fighting in China and the Soviet Union, and British activity near Thailand. A long commentary defends Japan’s economic controls and military readiness as responses to encirclement. A segment addressed to children in Hawaii praises Japanese air raids on Chongqing and aviation training.

subfiles.title: FBI cover letter forwarding Tokyo radio transcripts, August 11–15
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: The FBI forwards translated Tokyo broadcasts for August 11–15, 1941.
subfiles.summary: Forwards translated Tokyo radio transcripts for August 11–15.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, August 11, 1941
subfiles.about: The broadcast reports British preparations near Thailand, wartime news, and Japanese claims of economic resilience.
subfiles.summary: Reports cover fighting in China and Europe, British forces near Thailand, effects of freezing orders, and a rumored Axis conference. A weekly review recalls the landing in southern French Indochina. Shinichi Nanjo argues that Japanese rationing reflects planned economy rather than shortages.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, August 12, 1941
subfiles.about: The program frames the growing crisis around Thailand as the result of British and American policy.
subfiles.summary: News items cover Japanese troops in French Indochina, the Shanghai Battle anniversary, raids in China, conditions in Davao, and fighting in Europe. The long commentary claims Britain and the United States shifted their pressure from French Indochina to Thailand and calls for wider East Asian cooperation under Japan.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, August 13, 1941
subfiles.about: The broadcast commemorates the Shanghai Battle and comments on French Indochina and Thailand.
subfiles.summary: Reports cover Shanghai Battle ceremonies, Japanese air operations, Chiang Kai-shek’s statement, Thai neutrality, and fighting near Odessa. A poorly recorded commentary blames Britain and the United States for the East Asian crisis.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, August 14, 1941
subfiles.about: Only fragments of the broadcast were intelligible because of poor reception.
subfiles.summary: Audible fragments mention Hiranuma, Australia, Singapore, a Japanese air raid, and Chongqing.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, August 15, 1941, opening page
subfiles.about: The opening page reports a Japanese diplomatic appointment and reactions to the Roosevelt–Churchill declaration.
subfiles.summary: Reports Eiji Amau’s appointment and Japanese, Nanjing, and Chongqing reactions to the eight-point declaration.
